questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Center of Mass of a Rod
questions.problem: Consider a thin rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $0\le x\le 1$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)=x-{x}^{3}.$ Given that the rod's mass is $\frac{1}{4}$ units, what is the $x$-coordinate of its center of mass?
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass, denoted $\overset{―}{x},$ of a rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)$ is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the mass of the rod,

- ${M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}\,x\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the moment of the rod about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=x-{x}^{3},\,a=0,\,b=1.
$$

So, the moment of the rod about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot (x-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}-{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5} \\  & =\frac{2}{15}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{(\frac{2}{15})}{(\frac{1}{4})}=\frac{8}{15}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Center of Mass of a Rod
questions.problem: Consider a thin rod along the $x$-axis over the interval $0\le x\le 2$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)=8-{x}^{3}.$ Find the $x$-coordinate of the center of mass of the rod.
questions.worked_solution:
The center of mass of a rod placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $a\le x\le b$ whose mass density function is $\lambda (x)$ is given by 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m},
$$

 

where 

- $m={\int }_{a}^{b}\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the mass of the rod,

- ${M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}\,x\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x$ is the moment of the rod about the origin $O.$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=8-{x}^{3},\,a=0,\,b=2.
$$

So, the mass of the rod is

$$
\begin{aligned}m & ={\int }_{0}^{2}8-{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[8x-\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =8\cdot 2-\frac{1}{4}\cdot 16 \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

 

and the moment of the rod about the origin is

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot (8-{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}8x-{x}^{4}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[4{x}^{2}-\frac{1}{5}{x}^{5}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =4\cdot 4-\frac{1}{5}\cdot 32 \\  & =\frac{48}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\overset{―}{x}=\frac{{M}_{O}}{m}=\frac{(\frac{48}{5})}{12}=\frac{4}{5}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Moment of a Rod About the Origin
questions.problem: A thin rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)=\frac{4}{{x}^{3}},$ measured in $\text{kg/m},$ is placed along the $x$-axis over the interval $1\le x\le 4,$ where $x$ is measured in meters. Find the moment of the rod about the origin.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)$ for $a\le x\le b$ is given by 

$$
{M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=\frac{4}{{x}^{3}},\,a=1,\,b=4.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{1}^{4}x\cdot \frac{4}{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{4}{x}]}_{1}^{4} \\  & =-(\frac{4}{4}-\frac{4}{1}) \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required moment is $3\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.$

The thin rod above has the mass density function $\lambda (x)=\frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{kg/m}.$ Find the moment of the rod about the origin.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)$ for $a\le x\le b$ is given by 

$$
{M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)=\frac{2}{{x}^{2}},\,a=1,\,b=3.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{1}^{3}x\cdot \frac{2}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{2}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =[2\operatorname{ln}⁡x]_{1}^{3} \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡3-2\operatorname{ln}⁡1 \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡3.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required moment is $2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.$

The thin rod above has the mass density function $\lambda (x)={x}^{2}-x\,\text{kg/m}.$ Find the moment of the rod about the origin.
questions.worked_solution:
The moment about the origin $O$ of a rod with mass density function $\lambda (x)$ for $a\le x\le b$ is given by 

$$
{M}_{O}={\int }_{a}^{b}x\,\lambda (x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\lambda (x)={x}^{2}-x,\,a=1,\,b=3.
$$

We calculate the moment of the rod about the origin as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{M}_{O} & ={\int }_{1}^{3}x\cdot ({x}^{2}-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{3}-{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{x}^{4}}{4}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =(\frac{{3}^{4}}{4}-\frac{{3}^{3}}{3})-(\frac{{1}^{4}}{4}-\frac{{1}^{3}}{3}) \\  & =\frac{34}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the required moment is $\frac{34}{3}\,\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}.$
